# Temple Scroll Column 55 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 55 where the three translators significantly diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 55:4 — "righteousness" rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "to you it shall be righteousness" | Literal word order preserving Hebrew emphasis |
| LOGOS | "it shall be counted as righteousness for you" | Standard English rendering with clarified subject |
| PNEUMA | "the LORD your God will regard this as a righteous act" | Interpretive — specifies the divine evaluation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. Preserves the concept without EMET's awkward word order or PNEUMA's theological expansion.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 55:5 — "sojourner" vs. "foreigner"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "sojourner" | Standard rendering of ger — resident alien with legal protections |
| LOGOS | "sojourner" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "foreigner" | More accessible modern term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "sojourner" (EMET/LOGOS). The ger is not merely a "foreigner" (nokhri) but a resident alien with specific legal rights in Israelite law. The distinction matters.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 55:7 — "fathers/sons" vs. "parents/children"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "fathers... sons" | Literal Hebrew avot/banim |
| LOGOS | "fathers... sons" | Same — preserves the gendered language of the source |
| PNEUMA | "parents... children" | Gender-inclusive modern rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "fathers... sons" (EMET/LOGOS). The Hebrew text is specifically gendered and reflects the patrilineal legal framework. Gender-neutral rendering obscures the social context.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 55:14 — "declare-righteous/declare-guilty" vs. "acquitting/condemning" vs. "declare innocent/guilty"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "declare-righteous the righteous-one and declare-guilty the guilty-one" | Literal hiphil forms with Hebrew judicial vocabulary |
| LOGOS | "acquitting the innocent and condemning the guilty" | Standard English legal terminology |
| PNEUMA | "declare one innocent and the other guilty" | Simplified modern legal language |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "acquitting the innocent and condemning the guilty" (LOGOS). This captures the formal judicial process with appropriate English legal register.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 55:15-16 — "strokes" vs. "lashes" vs. corporal punishment terminology

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "strike him... strokes" | Literal nakkeh/makkot — from the root n-k-h "to strike" |
| LOGOS | "beaten... strokes" | Standard biblical rendering |
| PNEUMA | "flogged... lashes" | Modern criminal justice terminology |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "beaten... strokes" (LOGOS). "Flogged" and "lashes" (PNEUMA) evoke Roman punishment, which is anachronistic for this Israelite legal context. EMET's rendering is acceptable but LOGOS is smoother.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
